title: Factorized context superposition for held-out task combinations

task.train_mask: (procedure+domain) mod 4 != 0; every factor occurs in training

hypothesis: Binding reusable procedure and domain factors separately to low-description contexts permits held-out pair composition with useful quality and lower bytes than independently superposing each complete task vector.
physical_object: one shared superposition payload containing complete training tasks for native PSP, or two bound factor banks for compositional Mirror
mirror_coordinate: deterministic Rademacher procedure and domain addresses; unbind each then add
logical_multiplicity: 64 procedure×domain task functions, 16 held out during factor estimation
controls: native PA16-style random task context over 48 training combinations
compositional Mirror with two separately bound factor banks

development.allowed: implementation and metric-shape checks only; no fresh selection or access

storage.authority: actual torch-serialized inference payload bytes, all contexts, factor state and metadata charged

success_gate: Every fresh world: Mirror held-out NRMSE <=0.20, at least 20% below native PSP held-out retrieval, and payload <=80% of explicit bank; report plain factor-table control for Mirror-specific value.
failure_gate: Mirror held-out NRMSE >0.50 or no quality/byte benefit over generic factor table.
boundaries: Synthetic additive factor family only; not arbitrary task-model composition.
Combination count is not capacity; held-out output error is primary.
If generic factor table matches Mirror, only factor sharing is supported, not Mirror-specific benefit.

outcome_summary.interpretation: Factor sharing reconstructs the known additive family, but coordinatewise Mirror unbinding loses task quality; the simpler generic factor table is exact and uses fewer bytes.
